newsitem.title: USA: Delta to delay decision on pilot talks-union.
newsitem.headline: Delta to delay decision on pilot talks-union.

text.p: Delta Air Lines Inc will postpone a decision on whether to reopen contract talks with its pilots until after a new chief executive is named, the Delta pilots union said.

"With the impending change of leadership at Delta, management has stated that they want to delay making a decision reqarding this request until new CEO is in place," Delta's pilots union told its members in a recorded message.
Ronald Allen, Delta's chairman, chief executive and president, said last month he planned to retire in July. A successor has not yet been named.
The pilots union said last month they were seeking pay raises and work-rule changes only one year after ratifying the current four-year contract.
The Air Line Pilots Association said it was seeking the changes because of the recent financial strength of the third-largest U.S. airline and pay raises for pilots at rival airlines.
Delta representatives did not return calls seeking comment.
